obligations.note: Retention.java:22 now skips the legal-hold check for WITHDRAWN cases, so a withdrawn case on legal hold is purge-due after the retention period, which violates 'never while a legal hold applies'. The sample control test only covers declined cases, so its pass does not cover this path.

The change deviates from RET-1, and the exception register has no approved, unexpired exception for RET-1 or the mortgage.retention component (it holds only SES-1, LOG-1 and a withdrawn MFA-1 exception).
Ticket CHG-25519 is approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) on 2026-10-15, before the change opened on 2026-10-16. Its components [mortgage.retention] cover the only touched path, Retention.java.
The code_review approval is from declan.farrell@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author, Tomas Ortega.
The approval names head commit 36c9e2a, which is the only and final commit of the change.

The CI run on head 36c9e2a succeeded: 124 Jupiter tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the registered RET-1 control test controls.RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold. That test is labelled sample and only exercises declined cases. I could not rerun it locally because the JUnit jar is missing.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers Retention.java, so no previously accepted evidence lapses because of this change.

summary: The change edits one line of Retention.java so that a legal hold no longer blocks purging NPI for withdrawn cases. This directly violates RET-1, and no approved exception covers the deviation (EXC-1). The ticket, independent approval and CI records are otherwise in order, but CI passed only because the RET-1 control test samples declined cases and never a withdrawn case under hold. The change must be rejected.
